title: Chemical Equilibrium
short_title: Le Châtelier's principle, Keq and ICE tables
standard_text: Dynamic equilibrium can be shifted by changes to the surrounding conditions: reversible reactions, Le Châtelier's principle, the equilibrium constant Keq, ICE tables, and industrial applications. (summary of BC's Curriculum, Chemistry 12)
meta_desc: Free Chemistry 12 worksheets (BC Curriculum): Le Châtelier's principle, Keq and ICE tables. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: At equilibrium the forward and reverse rates are equal.
body_html:
How to think about it

In a closed system a reversible reaction reaches dynamic equilibrium: the forward and reverse rates are equal, so concentrations stay constant. Le Châtelier's principle: if a stress is applied (concentration, pressure, temperature), the equilibrium shifts to reduce it.

For aA + bB ⇌ cC + dD, Keq = [C]c[D]d ÷ ([A]a[B]b); pure solids and liquids are left out. A large Keq means mostly products. ICE tables find equilibrium concentrations.

Example

N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃. Which way does it shift if pressure increases?

Fewer gas molecules on the right

Answer: to the right

Example

Keq = 1 × 10⁻⁵. Mostly reactants or products?

K is very small.

Answer: mostly reactants

Common mistakes

  • Thinking reactions stop at equilibrium.
  • Putting solids or liquids in the Keq expression.
  • Thinking a catalyst changes the equilibrium position.

faq.q: What changes the value of Keq?
Why is ammonia made at high pressure?
faq.a: High pressure shifts the equilibrium toward NH₃, which has fewer gas molecules.

items.q: An engineer wants more NH<sub>3</sub> from making ammonia (Haber process): N<sub>2</sub> + 3H<sub>2</sub> ⇌ 2NH<sub>3</sub>, the energy change = −92 kJ. Which single change increases the amount of NH<sub>3</sub> at equilibrium?
c: The pressure is decreased (the container is made larger).
The pressure is increased (the container is made smaller).
items.e: Left: 4 mol gas, right: 2 mol gas. Higher pressure favors fewer gas moles; lower pressure favors more.

items.q: For 2NO₂(g) ⇌ N₂O₄(g), the brown colour fades when the mixture is cooled. What does this show?
items.e: Cooling favours the exothermic direction.

items.q: Why is the Haber process run at about 450 °C, even though a lower temperature gives more ammonia?
c: a lower temperature would make the rate too slow; 450 °C is a compromise
items.e: Yield and rate are balanced.

items.q: In blood, CO₂ + H₂O ⇌ H₂CO₃ ⇌ H⁺ + HCO₃⁻. What happens to blood pH if a person breathes too fast and loses CO₂?
c: pH rises, because the equilibria shift left and [H⁺] falls
items.e: This is respiratory alkalosis.

items.q: What effect does a catalyst have on an equilibrium?
c: it shifts equilibrium to the left
it shifts equilibrium to the right
it makes equilibrium reached faster but does not change its position or K
items.e: It speeds up both directions equally.
